Jo's sum of the first 50 positive integers is calculated using the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series:
\[
\text{Jo's sum} = \frac{50 \times 51}{2} = 1275
\]

Kate rounds each integer from 1 to 50 to the nearest multiple of 10 and then sums them. The numbers are grouped based on their rounding:
- Numbers 1-4 round to 0 (4 numbers)
- Numbers 5-14 round to 10 (10 numbers)
- Numbers 15-24 round to 20 (10 numbers)
- Numbers 25-34 round to 30 (10 numbers)
- Numbers 35-44 round to 40 (10 numbers)
- Numbers 45-50 round to 50 (6 numbers)

Calculating Kate's sum by multiplying the number of elements in each group by their rounded value:
\[
\begin{align*}
\text{Contribution from 1-4} & = 4 \times 0 = 0 \\
\text{Contribution from 5-14} & = 10 \times 10 = 100 \\
\text{Contribution from 15-24} & = 10 \times 20 = 200 \\
\text{Contribution from 25-34} & = 10 \times 30 = 300 \\
\text{Contribution from 35-44} & = 10 \times 40 = 400 \\
\text{Contribution from 45-50} & = 6 \times 50 = 300 \\
\end{align*}
\]

Summing these contributions:
\[
0 + 100 + 200 + 300 + 400 + 300 = 1300
\]

The positive difference between Jo's sum and Kate's sum is:
\[
|1275 - 1300| = 25
\]

Thus, the positive difference is \(\boxed{25}\).
